turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I've got her vitals from just now, blood pressure one thirty eight over eighty six, pulse seventy eight. She's outside talking about the parking.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Send her in.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ag, sorry, sorry, the robots by the mall were backed up all the way to the garage, I went round twice and nearly just went home. I'm here because I found a lump.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Where.

[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): In the left breast. Sunday, in the shower, I was soaping under my arm and my fingers stopped on a little knot, outer side, up towards the bra line. It doesn't hurt at all, I pressed it, I know that's silly, and there's no pain even when I lie on it.
[SEG0006] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Doctor, her sister was at reception before you called her. She said the lump has been there three weeks and it's sore when she lies on that side.

[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): No, hey, my sister does this, she answers for me and she gets it wrong. It is not sore. And it is not three weeks. I found it Sunday, that's four days, I remember because the geyser was acting up and the water went cold.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Four days or three weeks, noted. Nipple discharge?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): None whatsoever. I checked the cups of the bra, the towel, even the nightdress, nothing clear and nothing bloody, and I would have seen it, I was looking on purpose.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No. No fever. I've been a bit obsessive and checked with the thermometer, thirty six six, thirty six seven, nothing up.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough? Short of breath?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No cough. Breathing is the same as always, I walk the dog up the hill by the dam most mornings and I'm not more puffed than usual, even on the steep bit.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Weight up or down?

[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm. I don't actually know. The jeans feel a touch looser round the waist but our scale broke when we moved and I haven't replaced it, so I can't say I've lost weight, and I can't say I haven't. Sorry, that's a useless answer.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Medicines.

[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja. Amlodopine five milligrams in the morning for the pressure. The cholesterol one at night, atorvastin, twenty milligrams, for the cholesterol. Sugar tablets, glyclazide eighty milligrams with breakfast, for the sugar. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, half a teaspoon in warm water, nothing else herbal.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets.

[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Not mine. My husband takes metformin, a thousand milligrams twice a day, that's his, for his sugar, I don't take it. My sister is on biotin gummies for her hair, she offered me some, I said no.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Family. Breast cancer.

[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): My mother had breast cancer at fifty five. She had surgery and the tablets after, she's still alive, this was a good few years ago, I can never remember the exact year and it stresses me that I can't. My sister has not had it, she just panics.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Lie back.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Left upper outer breast, firm mobile lump, two centimetres, smooth. Not tender to pressure. No skin tethering, nipple normal. Right breast clear, no axillary nodes.

[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): Two centimetres, ok, because in the shower it felt like a marble, maybe one and a half, but I keep checking it at night and then it feels huge, and my hands are cold so I don't trust them. Are you sure the right side is empty, because at three a.m. I convince myself there's a matching one.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right side is clear. I can't say if this is a cyst or something serious.

[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): So not cancer? I'm forty six, my mother was fifty five, I did the sum in the car, nine years younger, and I have not slept a proper night since Sunday, just lying there counting.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not diagnosing cancer. It may be benign. It may not. Breast clinic, urgent.

[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Do I stop anything? I didn't take the amlodopine this morning, I was rushing, and some Sundays I forget it too, not every Sunday, just some, then I feel guilty. The powder is only turmeric and roots, the tub might say ashwagandha, I'm not a hundred percent sure, I can fetch it from the car.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Take today's amlodipine when you get home. Carry on the cholesterol tablet and the sugar tablet as usual. Leave the powder until the clinic tells you.

[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Even though it's just a shop remedy? My neighbour in Kempton got it from the Indian shop by the station, she says it's for stress, I started it in June for the sleeping, not for the lump. I don't want to mess up the scans.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave it. Bring the tub to the clinic. Urgent referral goes today. They will do a mammogram and an ultrasound.

[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): An ultrasound like for pregnancy? Because I had one of those years ago with my second, and the gel was freezing, I just want to know if it's the same machine or a breast one, sorry, that's probably a silly question.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breast ultrasound. Different probe. Provincial clinic, within two weeks.
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): We're on Discovery, hospital plan, the savings ran out in August, my husband does the paperwork. Does urgent mean they'll still see me if the medical aid argues?
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): The referral is to the provincial breast clinic. If the lump grows, or you get pain, or any nipple discharge, come back.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): And if I find another one on the right? I'll try not to prod. I will prod. I know I will.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): If something new appears, come back as well. Stop prodding.
[SEG0038] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll print the referral and put the clinic number on it.
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Thanks. I really did go on. The meter outside is definitely expired.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): Out via the desk.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Dose, oral route, morning use, since June, and sleep are stated; current use contradicted by advice to leave it.
bad.text: Ayurvedic powder (dose=half a teaspoon, route=oral, frequency=in the morning, duration=since June, indication=sleep, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Patient explicitly denied that the left breast lump is painful or sore, including when lying on it; the recorded facts instead list breast soreness as present from clinical staff despite the patient's correction.
Temperature details were stated with the fever denial: patient had checked at home and reported readings of 36.6 to 36.7.
Weight change was asked and not established: patient said jeans feel a bit looser but she cannot say whether she has lost weight because the scale is broken.
Physical exam included lump size and character not fully captured: left upper outer breast lump was 2 cm and smooth.
Examination found the right breast clear, separate from no axillary nodes.
Doctor specifically said he was not diagnosing cancer, that it may be benign and may not be.
Medication adherence detail missing: patient had not taken amlodipine that morning and sometimes forgets it on Sundays.
